What each field records

Reference
Use the same item ID as the schedule.
Item
Describe the selection without treating it as an order.
Quantity
Use the quantity appropriate to the unit.
Unit
Keep items, modules, and area units distinct.
Unit cost
Enter a verified price or clearly identified allowance.
Additional allowance
Record combined additional amounts; explain what is included in the notes.
Estimated total
Quantity × unit cost + additional allowance. Calculated only when quantity and unit cost exist.
Budget allowance
Enter the comparison budget in the same currency.
Remaining / (over)
Budget allowance minus estimated total. Negative means over the entered allowance.
Notes
Record quote source, currency, exclusions, and date.

How to use this template

Choose one currency for the workbook and replace all illustrative figures with project-specific inputs. Enter additional costs as amounts, not assumed tax percentages. Blank quantities or prices leave the calculated total blank; zero is a deliberate numeric input.

  1. Set a currency and list the items in scope.
  2. Replace example rates with dated quotes or explicitly labeled allowances.
  3. Review negative variance and unresolved inputs before discussing a project total.

Review before use

  • Do not add mixed currencies or unlike area units.
  • A blank line is unresolved, not a zero-cost item.
  • Do not treat the example total as a complete renovation budget.

Make it your own

One workbook with Instructions, Blank Template, and Worked Example sheets. Twenty editable rows; duplicate or extend the template for your project.
